main_text.p: fas est hominem homini insi-diari , ita hominem homini D de Reg.jur. Anton. Matth. tract. de Crim.tit. opem ferre & auxilium, fas sit & æquum.

Quimimo uti nefas est no-cere patriæ, ita & civi,quoni-5.1 48. c. am pars patriæ est. Quod si nocere nefas, etiam opitulari 2.n.12. Senec.2. de trâ.31. fas erit. Neque enim membra inter se consentiunt, neque pa-l.2,3. D. de just & jur.l.7.in fin.D de Serv.Ex-portand. triæ succurrunt, ad quod omni jure tenentur, nisi ad singulo-rum civium concurrant defen-sionem: quod singulos servari interest universi. Ne dicam, quod de jure civili nihil refe-rat, an quis ipsi sibi succurrat[?], an proximo, cui vis infertur.
Ut si ad defensionem sui ipsius Arg. l.8. §. fin. D. quod met.caus. recte occidat aggressorem, id liceat ad defensionem proximi, in dubio vitæ discrimine constituti.
Quid quod ille, qui damnum non prohibet, quod prohibere potuisset, quodque fieri passus est, l.45. in princ. D. Ad l. A-quil.

page.notes: Marginal references are grouped by line position in the right margin. The text is printed with long s, read here as s; "interfit" and "servari" read as intersit and servari. The first word of the page, "succurrat", is partly unclear in the scan: the letters are doubtful, so it is marked [?]. The word "sibi" is also doubtful. Marginal notes are split across lines in the scan and have been joined into one note each. The reference "quod" beside "recte" is part of the first note. The line "est," is set right-aligned.
